exposure: maternal COVID-19 mRNA monovalent primary vaccination series during pregnancy
maternal COVID-19 mRNA booster vaccination during pregnancy
maternal COVID-19 mRNA booster vaccination postpartum
outcome: maternal SARS-CoV-2-binding and functional antibody responses (IgG, nAb) at delivery and 2 months postpartum
infant SARS-CoV-2-binding and functional antibody responses (IgG, nAb) at delivery and 2 months of age
breast milk spike and receptor-binding domain IgG and IgA titers
cohort: The study included 237 maternal/infant dyads where mothers received COVID-19 mRNA monovalent vaccination during pregnancy, with some receiving a booster dose during pregnancy or within 2 months postpartum.
finding: mRNA COVID-19 monovalent booster vaccination during pregnancy results in significantly higher maternal and infant serum-binding IgG and nAb titers compared to a primary 2-dose series, including against Omicron variants, through 2 months of age.
